p: To the Members of the New York City Council: On behalf of The Ali Forney Center and the LGBTQIA+ unhoused youth and staff we represent across New York City, we submit this testimony in strong opposition to the proposed changes to the City Council’s internal rules that would consolidate more power in the Speaker’s office at the expense of individual Council Members and, by extension, the communities they represent. 1. Weakening Council Member Independence The proposed changes would strip away members’ ability to act independently in advancing legislation. Eliminating the independent bill-drafting unit and making it harder for members to bring legislation to a vote without the Speaker’s approval would silence the voices of New Yorkers whose Council Members seek to represent their needs. Communities deserve to know that their elected representatives can move legislation forward without being blocked by a single office. 2. Reducing Transparency and Accountability Rules that limit committee chairs’ authority over their own staff, and that weakens deadlines for bill drafting, reduce transparency, and make it harder for the public to follow and influence the legislative process. Our communities need more access to how decisions are made—not less. 3. Undermining Voter Power The Speaker is not elected by voters citywide. Voters elect their individual Council Members to represent them and to actively legislate on issues that directly impact their lives. Centralizing more power in the Speaker’s office removes power from voters and concentrates it in one office that is less directly accountable to the public.

4. Reversing Needed Reforms Past reforms sought to correct a history of heavy-handed leadership that stifled member independence and delayed key legislation—like paid sick leave. Rolling back these reforms risks taking the Council backwards to a system where community-driven priorities can be buried for political convenience. We urge the Council to reject proposed rule changes R. 7.60, 6.60(d) and (e), 8.220, 6.20(e), 10.50(b). Instead, the Council should focus on strengthening democracy, transparency, and accountability to the people of New York. Grassroots organizations and everyday New Yorkers rely on a Council where every member can legislate, deliberate, and advocate freely for their communities. Respectfully Submitted, Nadia Swanson, LCSW Director of Advocacy and Global Programs nswanson@aliforneycenter.org

Written Testimony Mohamed Q. Amin, Founder and Executive Director, Caribbean Equality Project
To the Members of the New York City Council:

My name is Mohamed Q. Amin, Executive Director of the Caribbean Equality Project (CEP), an immigrant rights organization that empowers, advocates for, and represents Afro and Indo-Caribbean LGBTQ+ people in New York City. For a decade, the organization has focused on advocacy for LGBTQ+ and immigrant rights, gender equity, racial justice, immigration, and mental health services through public education, community organizing, civic engagement, storytelling, and cultural and social programming to end hate violence in the Caribbean diaspora.

On behalf of the LGBTQ+ immigrant communities and Caribbean neighborhoods we have served and represented across New York City for a decade, we submit this testimony in strong opposition to the proposed changes to the City Council's internal rules that would consolidate more power in the Speaker's office at the expense of individual Council Members and, by extension, the communities they represent.

1. Weakening Council Member Independence The proposed changes would strip away members' ability to act independently in advancing legislation. Eliminating the independent bill-drafting unit and making it harder for members to bring legislation to a vote without the Speaker's approval would silence the voices of New Yorkers whose Council Members seek to represent their needs. Communities deserve to know that their elected representatives can move legislation forward without being blocked by a single office.

2. Reducing Transparency and Accountability Rules that limit committee chairs' authority over their own staff, weaken deadlines for bill drafting, reduce transparency, and make it harder for the public to follow and influence the legislative process. Our communities need more access to how decisions are made—not less.

Voters elect their individual Council Members to represent them and to actively legislate on issues that directly impact their lives. Centralizing more power in the Speaker’s office removes power from voters and concentrates it in one office that is less directly accountable to the public.

4. Reversing Needed Reforms Past reforms sought to correct a history of heavy-handed leadership that stifled member independence and delayed key legislation—like paid sick leave. Rolling back these reforms risks taking the Council backwards to a system where community-driven priorities can be buried for political convenience.

We unequivocally urge the Council to reject proposed rule changes R. 7.60, 6.60(d) and (e), 8.220, 6.20(e), 10.50(b). In Solidarity & Respect,

Mohamed Q. Amin Founder & Executive Director Caribbean Equality Project

The People’s Plan NYC, To the Members of the New York City Council: As a New Yorker and constituent, I strongly oppose the proposed changes to the City Council’s rules that would concentrate more power in the Speaker’s office and take independence away from individual Council Members. These changes would make it harder for everyday people like me—and the grassroots groups we are part of—to have a real voice in our city government. 1. Limiting Our Representation As constituents, we elect our Council Members to represent our local communities and fight for the issues we care about. If the Speaker’s office can stop bills from being drafted, or make it harder for Council Members to bring them to a vote, then my community’s concerns may never even get debated. I am concerned that this reduces the voice of constituents and makes it harder for us to move legislation that addresses local needs. 2. Reducing Transparency The proposed rules would weaken committee chairs’ authority and remove deadlines for bill drafting, making the process less open and less accountable. As a New Yorker, I want more transparency in government, not less. I am also concerned that no clear deadlines for legislation will mean that local community priorities will get stuck in legislative purgatory if not politically expedient for the Speaker. 3. Taking Power Away From Voters The Speaker is not elected by ordinary New Yorkers—we only get to elect our own Council Members. These proposed rules take power away from the people we actually vote for and give it to someone we don’t vote for. That undermines the whole point of local representation. 4. Risk of Stalling Important Community Legislation In the past, Council rules reforms made sure that bills supported by a majority of members could not be blocked forever. Rolling back those reforms risks returning us to a time when crucial issues—like paid sick leave—could be held up because leadership didn’t want them to move. I urge you to reject these rule changes [specifically R. 7.60, 6.60(d) and (e), 8.220, 6.20(e), 10.50(b)] and the representation of local constituencies and our issues. New Yorkers deserve a Council where every member can represent their communities freely, not one where decisions are controlled by a single leader not elected by constituencies across the city. Zara Nasir Queens, NY 11372
